sections.label: A
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.citation: CY 2022 AAR, Executive Summary, Section A, p. i
sections.text:
The City of Manila was founded on June 24, 1571, as a municipal government. It became the first chartered City by virtue of the Philippine Commission Act 183 on July 31, 1901, and gained autonomy with the passage of Republic Act (RA) No. 409 or the “Revised Charter of the City of Manila” on June 18, 1949.
The personnel complement of the City in Calendar Year (CY) 2022 totaled 19,178 composed of the following:

sections.label: D
sections.heading: Scope and Objectives of Audit
sections.citation: CY 2022 AAR, Executive Summary, Section D, p. iii
sections.text: The audit covered the accounts and operations of the City of Manila for the period January 1 to December 31, 2022. The audit aimed to: (a) lend credence to Management’s assertions on the financial statements; (b) recommend agency improvement opportunities; (c) determine compliance with existing laws, rules and regulations; and (d) determine the extent of implementation of prior years’ audit recommendations.

sections.label: E
sections.heading: Independent Auditor’s Report on the Financial Statements
sections.citation: CY 2022 AAR, Executive Summary, Section E, pp. iii-iv
sections.text:
The Auditor rendered a qualified opinion on the fairness of presentation of the financial statements due to the deficiencies noted in the audit that materially affected the balances/totals of certain accounts, which are discussed in detail in Part II of the report and summarized as follows:
1. The inventory accounts were overstated by a net amount of P32.595 million due to accounting errors in record keeping, non-maintenance of inventory records and unreconciled records of the Office of the City Accountant (OCAT) and City General Services Office (CGSO) contrary to Paragraph 27 of the International Public Sector Accounting Standards 1. This condition weighed on the fairness of the presentation of the inventories in the Financial Statement.
We recommended and Management agreed that:
a. OCAT correct the accounting errors in record-keeping; and
b. OCAT and City Government Services Office: (a) maintain the prescribed inventory records and information that will enable effective and efficient tracking of the movements of inventories; and (b) reconcile their inventory records periodically.
2. The accuracy and completeness of the Real Property Tax (RPT) and Special Education Tax (SET) Receivables and related Deferred Credit accounts as at year end of P11.388 billion, P5.941 billion and P4.791 billion, respectively, could not be established because access to the application system tracking these accounts was not granted to the Audit Team contrary to COA Circular No. 2020-010 dated December 2, 2020.
We recommended and Management agreed to provide the Audit Team access to the City Treasurer’s Office application system that tracks the RPT and SET accounts.
The aforementioned observations together with the corresponding recommendations were discussed with Management officials concerned during the Exit Conference on April 20, 2023. Management views and comments were incorporated in the report, where appropriate.

sections.label: F
sections.heading: Summary of Suspensions, Disallowances and Charges as of Year-end
sections.citation: CY 2022 AAR, Executive Summary, Section F, p. iv
sections.text: The audit suspensions, disallowances and charges amounting to P42.538 million, P67.200 million and P33.047 million, respectively, remained unsettled by the concerned officers/employees and third parties determined to be liable thereto due to the inability of the Management to fully enforce settlement of the same as required under Section 7.1.1 of COA Circular No. 2009-006 dated September 15, 2009.

sections.label: G
sections.heading: Status of Implementation of Prior Years’ Audit Recommendations
sections.citation: CY 2022 AAR, Executive Summary, Section G, p. iv
sections.text: Of the 53 prior years’ audit recommendations contained in the CYs 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 and 2021 Annual Audit Reports, eight or 15.10 per cent were fully implemented, 27 or 50.94 per cent were partially implemented and 18 or 33.96 per cent were unimplemented.
